title: AP-MALDI MSI of lipids in mouse brain tissue sections
protocol: Fix mouse brain on cryosectioning holder.
Cut 20 µm tissue sections at -25°C.
Transfer tissue sections onto glass slides before measurement or store the slides at -80°C until measurement.
Fix sample on a MALDI target plate with double-sided sticker.
Mark the region of interest with a colored pen.
Dissolve matrix DHB 30 mg/ml and CHCA 7 mg/ml in 1 ml 1:1 (v/v) acetone/water mixture containing 0.1% TFA.
Apply 80 µl matrix solution using a pneumatic sprayer system at a flow rate of 10 µl/min, sample rotation speed of 350 rpm and gas pressure of 1 bar.
Check matrix layer quality, crystal size, and homogeneous coverage with an optical microscope.
Calibrate m/z scale of mass spectrometer.
Mount MALDI target with sample on the target support of the AP-SMALDI MSI source.
Search region of interest with the optical sample observation camera.
Set the mass spectrometer to a mass range of m/z 300-1200.
Fix injection time to 500 ms.
Apply 4 kV to the MALDI target.
Set laser settings to 30 laser pulses per spot/pixel with a repetition rate of 60 Hz.
Focus laser outside the region of interest by maximizing the intensity and simultaneously lowering the laser pulse energy.
Identify the focal plane by inspection of the resulting MALDI mass spectra.
Set the step size (lateral resolution) of the measurement in the control software of the AP-SMALDI MSI source, e.g., 10 µm and corresponding number of pixels, e.g., 500x500.
Adjust laser pulse energy to a value that allows measuring with the set lateral resolution.
Start data acquisition and the MSI experiment in the control software of the MSI source.
Load mass spectrometric data and imaging data with the MIRION imaging software.
Set image bin width to m/z ±0.01.
Export all relevant images with their corresponding intensity weighted centroid m/z value as .jpg and as a .csv file, respectively.
Combine three different ion images into a red-green-blue (RGB) overlay image.
Generate all MS images without further image processing steps such as smoothing or interpolation.
Normalize MS images to the base pixel (highest intensity) per image (m/z bin).
Import the m/z value list (*.csv file) into a database (e.g., METLIN).
Search for database entries within a search window of 2 ppm for accurate mass compound assignment.

Dehydrate the sample in ethanol and gradually increase the demineralized water content: Incubate with 100% ethanol for 2 min, then with 70% ethanol for 2 min, followed by 40% ethanol for 2 min, and finally rinse with demineralized water for 2 min.
Stain the sample with hematoxylin for 12 min.
Wash the sample with tap water for 10 min, then wash with demineralized water for 5 min.
Apply a 1% aqueous Eosin Y solution to the sample for 1 min.

Differentiate in demineralized water and gradually increase the ethanol content: Rinse with demineralized water for 2 min, then with 40% ethanol for 2 min, followed by 70% ethanol for 2 min, and finally rinse with 100% ethanol for 2 min.
Rinse the sample with xylol for 2 min.
Fixate the sample with eukitt between glass slides.
